codeReview.summary: The step executor implementation is solid, well-structured, and covers all 9 validation assertions (VAL-QUEUE-024..029, 032..034). The factory function pattern with full DI follows existing project conventions. Sequential processing, worker crash isolation, evaluator graceful degradation, budget checking, shutdown support, revision loop, and handoff chaining all work correctly. 35 comprehensive tests cover all expected behaviors plus edge cases. Two non-blocking issues found: (1) an unused EXECUTOR_PROVENANCE constant, and (2) validationCriteria from the dispatcher return value is captured but never forwarded to the evaluator — the existing ExecutionLoop passes validation_criteria to the evaluator, so when integrating the real evaluator later, the EvaluatorFn type signature will need to accept validation criteria. Neither issue blocks functionality since the DI types can be adjusted at integration time.

issues.description: EXECUTOR_PROVENANCE constant is defined but never used. Only makeProvenance() is used throughout the file. Dead code that should be removed.

DispatcherFn returns { prompt, validationCriteria } but validationCriteria is destructured in executeStep (line 297) and immediately discarded — only 'prompt' is used. The existing ExecutionLoop (execution-loop.ts:652) passes validation_criteria from the dispatcher decision to evaluator.evaluate(). When integrating the real evaluator, the EvaluatorFn signature will need updating to accept validation criteria, or the executor must pass it through. This is a design gap that will surface during integration.

The 'revision prompt includes evaluator feedback' test only asserts that prompts[1] contains 'MISSING_TESTS' (the reason). It does not verify that feedback ('ADD_UNIT_TESTS') and suggestions ('WRITE_JEST_TEST') are also present in the revision prompt. The implementation correctly includes all three, but the test coverage for this behavior is partial.
